parameters.definition: protocol-rules.md 3.2: channel = data_processes.channel_id raw value; path = channels from the start step (DEPEND_PROCESS_ID exactly NONE after ASCII space/tab/CR/LF trim) along the DEPEND chain to each end step; consecutive equal channels are not merged; one path per end step when branching
parameters.reasonRule: one reason per excluded transaction: smallest protocol-rules.md 3.2 step, ties by the 3.4 table order (graph_truncated first) - protocol-rules.md 3.4 full reason selection order
parameters.countingRule: transactions with a TRANSACTION row only, latest revision per execution (same rows as relation candidates). A path is counted once per transaction even if several end steps give the same channels. ratio = path transactions / pathTransactions (branching transactions add to several paths, so ratios can sum above 1). excludeProcessIds is not applied (Detector judges with all PROCESS rows)
parameters.unitNote: excludedReasons counts transactions only. PROCESS rows without TRANSACTION_ID (protocol-rules.md 3.4 transaction_id_missing) are not grouped into transactions and are counted as rows in transactionIdMissingRows (each such row is its own unkeyed node in the graph)
parameters.endpointRule: endpoint_mismatch (information only, not an exclusion): representative TRANSACTION row start_channel_id/end_channel_id raw values vs first/last channel of every path. Not compared when either value is absent or the representative row is ambiguous
parameters.selectionPolicy: no automatic adoption: observed paths are listed for the user to confirm and save. status insufficient_evidence when pathTransactions < minTransactions (display only)
parameters.outputLimitRule: per interface, paths sorted by transactions desc then pathKey (code point) asc; only the first maxOutputPaths are listed (protocol-rules.md 4 save limit: 64 paths per entry), the rest are summarized in omittedPaths {paths, transactions}. ratio, rare, status and distinctPaths use all paths before the cut. omittedPaths.transactions is the sum of per-path transaction counts, so a branching transaction can be counted more than once
